terra.problem: David says he has no rest at night; the verse does not say he cannot sleep.
Saying David is reminding himself gives a purpose the psalm does not state.
The verse says God has been David’s God from the womb, not that David personally trusted Him before he could speak.
The verse says there is no one to help, not that nobody else is close.
Saying David has nothing left in the tank stretches the pictures of being poured out and having strength dried up.
The boxing joke makes David’s description of his suffering the joke.
The verse does not say David is standing while his garments are divided.
Clothes off his back suggests the garments were taken from him while he was wearing them; the verse does not say that.
Saying David is not worried about his name asserts a feeling the verse does not give.
A cookie box that never runs out adds an endless supply to the psalm’s promise that the poor will eat and be satisfied.
Kings waiting their turn adds a detail the verse does not give.
